correctness.rationale: The exact cell-image graph gives one-level first descent F=z(2/3+sF³/3). Uniform initial I0 maps under τ1 to depth j with probability 2^{-j-1}, under τ2 to opposite depth 2; hence H=2z/[3(2-F)]+zsF²/3. Every return itinerary is an affine full branch onto the terminal I0, establishing conditional uniformity and independent renewal increments. Evaluating at s=-1 and z=1 gives the stated cubic root and side eigenvalue. The singular unmarked cubic at z=1 yields 1-H(z,1)~(4/3)√(1-z), so monotone Tauberian theorem gives 4/(3√πn) tail. A finite exact-rational checker passes 113 comparisons, supplementing the proof.

value.rationale: The source emphasizes two neutral attracting endpoints whose orbits switch sides, making the induced left/right transport at the central junction a natural missing observable. A full two-state Markov-renewal law quantifies *both* temporal intermittency (infinite-mean sqrt tail) and spatial memory loss per junction return (strict geometric eigenvalue); neither occupation-time Darling–Kac limits nor unmarked hitting transforms give these two scales simultaneously. The claim covers the complete natural central-return kernel, not a cherry-picked period or finite test.
